result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers cover every rubric point with near-identical concrete fixes: a compact heading with the result count, the delivery promise moved sitewide, 3–5 filter groups expanded per category, sticky filters, 4 columns with spec, pack and stock on each card, and a filter drawer with 2 columns on phones. A adds min-width wrapping and empty-state planning, while B adds per-unit pricing and a quantity field on the card. Neither spends time on visual styling, so neither is clearly better overall. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers cover every rubric item with concrete layout changes. Each recommends cutting the banner to a compact heading, collapsing the filters to a few category-specific groups, moving to 4 columns with spec-rich cards, and putting filters behind a 'Filter & sort' sheet on phones. B is slightly better: it separates the diagnosis from the fixes more clearly, plans for empty states and edge cases, and suggests an analytics split that would show whether the listing page or the product page is losing sales.
